notes: ABIs: arm64-v8a only. Every other enginehost plugin ships x86_64 beside it; this one cannot. The wall is cocos2d-x 3.17.2, the framework this engine renders and runs on. Its dependency set is not built from source: external/<lib>/CMakeLists.txt in the cocos2d-x deps package declares each one as an IMPORTED static library at prebuilt/android/${ANDROID_ABI} (cmake/CocosExternalConfig.cmake:33), and the whole v3-deps line of cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-bin -- every tag from the v3-deps-158 that cocos2d-x 3.17.2 pins through the last one, v3-deps-172 -- contains exactly three Android ABIs: armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a and x86. There is no x86_64 anywhere in it. Nine of the libraries this engine links come from that set (z, png, webp, tiff, freetype, chipmunk, BulletCollision, BulletDynamics, LinearMath), so on x86_64 they simply do not exist. Upstream's own builder for that set cannot make them either: cocos2d-x-3rd-party-libs-src branch v3, build/android.ini, says cfg_all_supported_arches=("armv7" "x86" "arm64" "mips") and defines no x86_64 alias folder, host triple or API level. The rest of the port is mechanical by comparison: Kirikiroid2Yuri's script/_androida64.sh names aarch64-linux-android and -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a at every call site and would retarget, bar opencv's arm-only libtegra_hal.a (src/core/CMakeLists.txt:185, which x86_64 has no counterpart for) and ffmpeg's --arch=aarch64 --disable-asm. Building the nine cocos2d-x libraries from their own upstream sources for android-x86_64 and staging them into that prebuilt layout is the known route, and it is a port of a 2019 framework to an architecture it never shipped for, not an ABI flag.
